 Minnesota Wild Recalls Forward Hunter Haight and Defenseman Carson Lambos from Iowa
 By 
 Minnesota Wild 
 Wild.com 
 October 18, 2026 
 Link copied 
 SAINT PAUL, Minn. - Minnesota Wild President of Hockey Operations and General Manager Bill Guerin today announced the National Hockey League (NHL) club has recalled forward  Hunter Haight  and defenseman  Carson Lambos  from the Iowa Wild of the American Hockey League (AHL). The team also placed defenseman  Jared Spurgeon  on Injured Reserve.
 Haight, 22 (4/4/04), owns five points (3-2=5), four penalty minutes (PIM), a plus-four rating and eight shots on goal in six games with Iowa this season. He ranks first on Iowa in goals and plus/minus rating and second in points. He made his NHL debut last season at St. Louis on Oct. 9, 2025, and tallied one assist in seven games with Minnesota. The 5-foot-10, 187-pound native of Strathroy, Ontario, recorded 32 points (18-14=32), six power play goals (PPG) and 112 shots on goal last season with Iowa, ranking second on the team in goals and PPG and T-5th in points. He also represented Iowa at the 2026 AHL All-Star Classic.  Haight owns 71 points (41-30=71), 56 PIM, 13 PPG and 274 shots on goal in 127 games in three seasons with Iowa (2024-26). He was selected by Minnesota in the second round (No. 47 overall) of the 2022 NHL Draft and wears sweater No. 37 with the Wild.
 Lambos, 23 (1/14/03), owns two points (1-1=2), five PIM and ranks second on Iowa with 15 shots on goal in six games this season. He collected 19 points (8-11=19), 48 PIM and 111 shots on goal in 70 games with Iowa last season, ranking first among team defensemen in goals and third in points. The 6-foot-1, 191-pound native of Winnipeg, Manitoba, made his NHL debut at Columbus on Dec. 18, 2025, recording a plus-1 rating, one a shot on goal and one blocked shot in 10:16 of time on ice (TOI). For his career, Lambos has skated in 213 career games over four AHL seasons with Iowa (2023-26), posting 54 points (18-36=54), 160 PIM and 301 shots on goal. Lambos was selected by Minnesota in the first round (No. 26 overall) of the 2021 NHL Draft and wears sweater No. 55 with Minnesota.
 The Wild hosts the Columbus Blue Jackets tonight at 7 5 p.m. on Wild+ and KFAN FM 100.3.
